item.text:
# 1B.9 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **moderately positive** on precaution, especially for cyber, AI, and critical digital infrastructure. Scholz and his government repeatedly framed these domains as security issues, backed regulation, and set transition timelines for risky infrastructure. **Transparency is mixed**: the direction is precautionary, but some 5G security talks were conducted confidentially. I found **no direct 2024 evidence** on biological-risk governance.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **National Security Strategy** | Federal Government | 14 Jun 2023, still operative in 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/aktuelles/national-security-strategy-2196356 | Scholz described Germany’s first National Security Strategy as a systematic, prevention-oriented approach that includes diplomacy, police, fire brigades, technical relief services, development cooperation, cyber security, and supply-chain resilience. It also explicitly mentions global pandemic prevention. This is the clearest background evidence for precaution in catastrophic-risk domains. | 1B.9, 1B.7 |
| **Bundeskanzler Scholz zur aktuellen Sicherheitslage** | Bundesregierung | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/scholz-sicherheitslage-2291096 | Scholz said German security authorities had carefully prepared for a high-risk summer and framed safety as a core state duty. This supports a cautious, institution-based handling of security risks rather than improvisation. | 1B.9, 1B.3, 1B.7 |
| **Germany to approve EU’s planned AI act** | Reuters | 30 Jan 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/germany-will-approve-eus-planned-ai-act--sources-3286730 | Reuters reported that the German government settled its internal dispute and moved to approve the EU AI Act, after a compromise that would preserve “trustworthy AI” while remaining innovation-friendly. This is good evidence that Scholz’s government handled AI regulation with precaution rather than deregulatory haste. | 1B.9 |
| **Germany agrees phaseout of Huawei, ZTE components in 5G core network** | Reuters | 11 Jul 2024 | https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DEUTSCHE-TELEKOM-AG-444661/news/Germany-agrees-phaseout-of-Huawei-ZTE-components-in-5G-core-network-47361811/ | Reuters reported that Germany completed contracts to remove Huawei and ZTE components from 5G core networks after 2026, with further network elements to be replaced by 2029. This is strong precautionary handling of dual-use digital infrastructure. | 1B.9 |
| **Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Oct 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/rede-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2307122 | Scholz said AI risks must not be ignored and argued that the EU AI Act creates a safer environment and stronger user trust. He also tied 5G security to removing critical components from high-risk networks on a fixed timetable. This is direct evidence of precaution plus a regulatory frame. | 1B.9, 1B.7 |
| **Insider - Regierung entscheidet "in Kürze" über Sicherheit im 5G-Netz** | Reuters | 23 May 2024 | https://www.onvista.de/news/2024/05-23-bericht-regierung-vertagt-entscheidung-ueber-strengere-vorschriften-im-5g-netz-0-20-26275293 | Reuters reported that the 5G security decision was handled through confidential interministerial talks, and the ministries declined public comment because of agreed confidentiality. This is the main transparency counterweight: the policy direction was precautionary, but the process was not fully transparent in real time. | 1B.9 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of a serious mis-handling of AI, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk domains on the scale of reckless deployment.
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** on biological-risk policy, pathogen security, gene editing, or biosecurity transparency.
- The strongest limitation is **process transparency**: the 5G security decision was partly negotiated behind closed doors, so the record is more precautionary than openly transparent.

## Synthesis for 1B.9

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz handled cyber and AI-related catastrophic-risk domains with real precaution.
- **Why:** he backed the AI Act, treated 5G supply-chain security as a state-security issue, and used a broader national-security framework that includes cyber security and pandemic prevention.
- **Transparency:** mixed rather than fully strong, because the 5G process was confidential and I did not find a comparable 2024 transparency record for biosecurity or frontier AI incident governance.
- **Overall:** moderately positive on precaution, weaker on transparency, and thin on biological-risk evidence.
